## IRouteWidgetEdit type

Widget route atom: forced single-widget edit.

**Signature:**

```typescript
type IRouteWidgetEdit = INeverFields<`rich` | `richOptions` | `broadcast` | `chunkSize` | `fallback` | `options` | `editOptions` | `fallbackOptions` | `is_shared`> & {
    mode: `edit`;
    keyboard?: IInlineKb | null;
};
```
**References:** [INeverFields](./gramstax.ineverfields.md)<!-- -->, [IInlineKb](./gramstax.iinlinekb.md)

## Remarks

Re-applies the template's `chat_data` / `public_data`<!-- -->, caption, and keyboard to the widget message held by the context — never the HTML, which the Bot API cannot replace. NOT atomic: up to three API calls (`editMessageWidgetData` / `editSharedWidgetData`<!-- -->, `editMessageCaption`<!-- -->, `editMessageReplyMarkup`<!-- -->), so a failure mid-way leaves part of the message updated. The keyboard slot is inline-only: `editMessageReplyMarkup` rejects a bottom keyboard.

On a shared widget the state edit goes to `editSharedWidgetData` (public data, every message showing the widget), while the caption and keyboard edits still target only the context-held message. Shared-ness is auto-detected from the context, so this route takes no `is_shared` field.
